extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven types of mathematical reasoning across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 math-targeted QA datasets and 19 VQA datasets), plus 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For MathQA datasets, up to 400 examples per source were collected (2,666 total). For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples with numeric answers or quantity words (4,949 candidates), then three expert annotators manually labeled them for mathematical reasoning using majority voting, limiting to 400 per source (2,739 final). The three new datasets (736 examples total) were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields with a two-step review process achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets covering GPS, MWP, and TQA tasks; 19 VQA datasets with math-related instances); puzzle test figures from online learning platforms (IQTest); functional plots (FunctionQA); and academic paper illustrations including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources and Huggingface papers (PaperQA). VQA datasets initially yielded 4,949 candidates before manual filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting. For new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields through a two-step process: initial independent annotation by three reviewers, followed by discussion among the entire review team to resolve discrepancies. Annotators were trained using detailed instructions with positive and negative examples, and provided three labeling options (Yes/No/Unsure). Human performance study used Amazon Mechanical Turk with annotators having >5,000 HIT tasks and >0.99 acceptance score, including qualification questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance evaluation; custom annotation tool (GUI) for labeling mathematical reasoning
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% for new datasets (only 6 disagreements among 736 questions). Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling, indicating substantial consistency among three annotators. Majority voting used to finalize VQA examples.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotators per item for new datasets and VQA mathematical reasoning labeling; five annotators per question for human performance evaluation on testmini subset
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new dataset annotation; Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with >5,000 HIT tasks completed and >0.99 acceptance score for human performance evaluation
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules for automatic selection of VQA examples: selected examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to sourcing from original data providers. Annotations lack unified format and structure due to heterogeneity of sources. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data. Scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have wide range of real-world applications, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery in advanced research fields.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks. It encompasses tasks including figure question answering (FQA), geometry problem solving (GPS), math word problem (MWP), textbook question answering (TQA), and visual question answering (VQA).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining potential data noise, in response to community feedback. They are committed to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models. In future iterations, the benchmark will encompass a broader array of problems and visual contexts, while also providing unified and comprehensive annotations.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage sampling strategy for testmini subset: (1) randomly sample questions with threshold of 4 for each source dataset; (2) randomly sample remaining questions proportionally to source dataset distribution in entire set
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Quality checks conducted to address unidentified errors

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Our benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, and we are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining the potential data noise, in response to the community feedback. rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: To ensure that each source dataset is well represented in testmini and to maintain a distribution in testmini closely resembling the whole set, we adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set.
